en: The Philippine flag has 8 rays on its sun, representing the first 8 provinces that revolted against Spanish colonial rule.
The Philippines celebrated Independence Day on July 4 from 1946 until 1964, when President Diosdado Macapagal changed it to June 12.
The Philippine Senate is composed of exactly 24 senators who are elected nationwide to serve a single 6-year term.
The Philippines has 185 distinct living languages, but only Filipino and English are designated as official languages for government and education.
Filipino biologist Angel Alcala discovered and cataloged over 50 new species of reptiles and amphibians during his decades of field research.
The Giant Lantern Festival in San Fernando features illuminated Christmas parols that can measure up to 20 feet in diameter.
Jose Rizal was only 35 years old when he was executed by firing squad at Bagumbayan on December 30, 1896.
The Philippine eagle stands about 3 feet tall and has a massive wingspan measuring up to 6.5 feet.
Under the 1987 Philippine Constitution, citizens must be at least 18 years old and registered to vote in national elections.
The Philippines is divided into 17 administrative regions, including the Cordillera Administrative Region and the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao.
The Panagbenga flower festival in Baguio City lasts for exactly one month, featuring massive float parades and daily street dancing.
The Banaue Rice Terraces, a famous cultural landscape, were carved into the mountains by the Ifugao people over 2,000 years ago.
